title: Your own limit
topic: Cap your repayments with your bank data

steps.title: "Parcelas: max 20% of my pay. The card bill: always in full."
steps.body: After the fridge, the stack and the rotativo, Rafa set two rules. They don't stop him buying things. They keep his [[committed-income]] small enough that one bad month doesn't roll into the next. His rules, not a recipe.

steps.prompt: Rafa earns R$2,800. His rule is "max 20% in installments". How much can he commit each month?
steps.explanation: 20% of R$2,800 is R$560. His four installments were R$710, so the rule would have said no to the last one.

steps.prompt: Why does "always pay the card bill in full" matter more than the exact limit?
options: Rolled-over card debt is usually the most expensive credit there is
Because the card stops working otherwise
Because paying in full earns interest
steps.explanation: The [[revolving-credit|rotativo]] grows on top of itself. Paying in full keeps the card a payment tool, not a loan.
